require 'redmine/scm/adapters/subversion_adapter'

module Redmine
  # @private
  module VERSION
    MAJOR = 5
    MINOR = 1
    TINY  = 13

    # Branch values:
    # * official release: nil
    # * stable branch:    stable
    # * trunk:            devel
    BRANCH = 'stable'

    # Retrieves the revision from the working copy
    def self.revision
      if File.directory?(File.join(Rails.root, '.svn'))
        begin
          path = Redmine::Scm::Adapters::AbstractAdapter.shell_quote(Rails.root.to_s)
          if `#{Redmine::Scm::Adapters::SubversionAdapter.client_command} info --xml #{path}` =~ /commit\s+revision="(\d+)"/
            return $1.to_i
          end
        rescue
          # Could not find the current revision
        end
      end
      nil
    end

    REVISION = self.revision
    ARRAY    = [MAJOR, MINOR, TINY, BRANCH, REVISION].compact
    STRING   = ARRAY.join('.')

    def self.to_a; ARRAY  end
    def self.to_s; STRING end
  end
end

    def self.included(base)
      base.extend ClassMethods
    end

    class << self
      def encrypt_text(text)
        if cipher_key.blank? || text.blank?
          text
        else
          c = OpenSSL::Cipher.new("aes-256-cbc")
          iv = c.random_iv
          c.encrypt
          c.key = cipher_key
          c.iv = iv
          e = c.update(text.to_s)
          e << c.final
          "aes-256-cbc:" + [e, iv].map {|v| Base64.strict_encode64(v)}.join('--')
        end
      end

      def decrypt_text(text)
        if text && match = text.match(/\Aaes-256-cbc:(.+)\Z/)
          if cipher_key.blank?
            logger.error "Attempt to decrypt a ciphered text with no cipher key configured in config/configuration.yml" if logger
            return text
          end
          text = match[1]
          c = OpenSSL::Cipher.new("aes-256-cbc")
          e, iv = text.split("--").map {|s| Base64.decode64(s)}
          c.decrypt
          c.key = cipher_key
          c.iv = iv
          d = c.update(e)
          d << c.final
        else
          text
        end
      end

      def cipher_key
        key = Redmine::Configuration['database_cipher_key'].to_s
        key.blank? ? nil : Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(key)[0..31]

require "concurrent/map"

module ActiveSupport
  # KeyGenerator is a simple wrapper around OpenSSL's implementation of PBKDF2.
  # It can be used to derive a number of keys for various purposes from a given secret.
  # This lets Rails applications have a single secure secret, but avoid reusing that
  # key in multiple incompatible contexts.
  class KeyGenerator
    class << self
      def hash_digest_class=(klass)
        if klass.kind_of?(Class) && klass < OpenSSL::Digest
          @hash_digest_class = klass
        else
          raise ArgumentError, "#{klass} is expected to be an OpenSSL::Digest subclass"
        end
      end

      def hash_digest_class
        @hash_digest_class ||= OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1
      end
    end

    def initialize(secret, options = {})
      @secret = secret
      # The default iterations are higher than required for our key derivation uses
      # on the off chance someone uses this for password storage
      @iterations = options[:iterations] || 2**16
      # Also allow configuration here so people can use this to build a rotation
      # scheme when switching the digest class.
      @hash_digest_class = options[:hash_digest_class] || self.class.hash_digest_class
    end

    # Returns a derived key suitable for use.  The default +key_size+ is chosen
    # to be compatible with the default settings of ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.
    # i.e. <tt>OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1#block_length</tt>
    def generate_key(salt, key_size = 64)
      OpenSSL::PKCS5.pbkdf2_hmac(@secret, salt, @iterations, key_size, @hash_digest_class.new)
    end
  end

  # CachingKeyGenerator is a wrapper around KeyGenerator which allows users to avoid
  # re-executing the key generation process when it's called using the same +salt+ and
  # +key_size+.
  class CachingKeyGenerator
    def initialize(key_generator)
      @key_generator = key_generator
      @cache_keys = Concurrent::Map.new
    end

    # Returns a derived key suitable for use.
    def generate_key(*args)
      @cache_keys[args.join("|")] ||= @key_generator.generate_key(*args)
    end
  end

steps.message: This is the central compatibility point. Rails 6.1 hardcodes PBKDF2-SHA1 for every derived key, while 7.0's `load_defaults` switches the digest to SHA256 through `key_generator_hash_digest_class`. Any secret-derived data would then stop verifying. I'll confirm how that config is wired, and check the 7.0 message-verifier and cookie code.

steps.message: The only cookie change between 6.1 and 7.0 is that 7.0 rescues `JSON::ParserError` on decrypt. That means if 7.0 is set to `:json` while Marshal cookies exist, the session is silently discarded and the user is signed out. So the Rails 7.0 release must not use `:json` until it can read Marshal cookies. Next I'll check Redmine's session verification and what happens on a CSRF failure, since that's another route to a sign-out.

The baseline passes on Ruby 3.0. The design is now clear enough to act on. The rollback-sensitive Rails 7.0 defaults are the cookie serializer, the key digest, and per-form CSRF tokens, and all three must be pinned.   # Return true if token has expired
  def expired?
    validity_time = self.class.invalid_when_created_before(action)
    validity_time.present? && created_on < validity_time
  end

  def max_instances
    Token.actions.has_key?(action) ? Token.actions[action][:max_instances] : 1
  end

  def self.invalid_when_created_before(action = nil)
    if Token.actions.has_key?(action)
      validity_time = Token.actions[action][:validity_time]
      validity_time = validity_time.call(action) if validity_time.respond_to? :call
    else

    end

    if validity_time
      Time.now - validity_time
    end
  end

    t = Token.arel_table

    # Unknown actions have default validity_time
    condition = t[:action].not_in(self.actions.keys).and(t[:created_on].lt(invalid_when_created_before))

# One-off generator: run on the R0 code (Rails 6.1 / Ruby 3.0) to capture
# artifacts that real users/mails would already carry.
class GenR0GoldenTest < Redmine::IntegrationTest
  OUT = '/tmp/gen/out'

  def test_generate
    FileUtils.mkdir_p OUT
    travel_to Time.utc(2025, 1, 16, 12, 0, 0) do

      mail_token = Mailer.mail_link_token(:unwatch, 'user_id' => 2, 'issue_id' => 1)

      puts "mail_token=#{mail_token[0, 40]}..."
      puts "session cookie bytes=#{cookies['_redmine_session'].bytesize} tk=#{tk}"
    end
  end
end

steps.message: The existing mail-link tests use `Mailer.mail_link_token` and `verify_mail_link`, and the header shows `#loggedas` for signed-in users. I'll write the compatibility tests now, based on the R0 goldens. They cover three things: the session still logs the user in, the unwatch link still works, and this release still writes R0-format cookies.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /app/test/fixtures/files/upgrade && cp /tmp/gen/r0/session_cookie.txt /app/test/fixtures/files/upgrade/r0_session_cookie.txt && cp /tmp/gen/r0/session_tk.txt /app/test/fixtures/files/upgrade/r0_session_token.txt && cp /tmp/gen/r0/mail_unwatch_token.txt /app/test/fixtures/files/upgrade/r0_mail_unwatch_token.txt && cat > /app/test/integration/release_compatibility_test.rb <<'EOF'
# frozen_string_literal: true

require File.expand_path('../../test_helper', __FILE__)

# Rolling upgrades and rollbacks between Redmine releases must not sign anyone
# out nor break a link in a mail that was already sent (see docs/UPGRADE.md).
#
# The files in test/fixtures/files/upgrade/ were produced by the previous
# release (Rails 6.1 on Ruby 3.0) and are artifacts that users already hold:
# a session cookie with its session token, and an unwatch link from an email.
# They must keep working on every release of this series.
class ReleaseCompatibilityTest < Redmine::IntegrationTest
  fixtures :projects, :users, :email_addresses, :roles, :members, :member_roles,
           :trackers, :projects_trackers, :issue_statuses, :enumerations, :issues,
           :enabled_modules, :watchers, :tokens

  # The golden artifacts were created on 2025-01-16 12:00 UTC. Mail links are
  # valid for 30 days, so verify them within that window.
  GOLDEN_TIME = Time.utc(2025, 1, 16, 12, 0, 0)

  def golden(name)
    File.read(Rails.root.join('test/fixtures/files/upgrade', name)).strip
  end

  def test_session_cookie_from_previous_release_keeps_user_logged_in
    travel_to GOLDEN_TIME do
      # The session token is stored in the database, so recreate that row.
      # insert_all skips Token's before_create, which would otherwise replace the value.
      Token.insert_all!([{:user_id => 2, :action => 'session', :value => golden('r0_session_token.txt'),
                          :created_on => Time.now, :updated_on => Time.now}])

      cookies['_redmine_session'] = golden('r0_session_cookie.txt')
      get '/my/account'

      assert_response :success
      assert_select '#loggedas', :text => /jsmith/
    end
  end

  def test_unwatch_link_from_previous_release_still_works
    travel_to GOLDEN_TIME do
      token = golden('r0_mail_unwatch_token.txt')
      assert_equal({'user_id' => 2, 'issue_id' => 1}, Mailer.verify_mail_link(token, :unwatch))

      Issue.find(1).set_watcher(User.find(2), true)
      assert Issue.find(1).watched_by?(User.find(2))

      get '/mail_links/unwatch', :params => {:token => token}

      assert_response :success
      assert_select 'p', :text => /no longer watching/
      assert_not Issue.find(1).watched_by?(User.find(2))
    end
  end

  def test_cookies_are_still_written_in_the_previous_release_format
    # Ops may roll this release back to the previous one, which can only read
    # the Marshal payload, legacy AES-256-CBC encryption and no cookie metadata.
    # Writing any newer format here would sign users out on rollback.
    log_user 'jsmith', 'jsmith'
    get '/my/account'
    assert_response :success

    raw = cookies['_redmine_session']
    assert raw.present?
    key_generator = Rails.application.key_generator
    config = Rails.application.config.action_dispatch
    secret = key_generator.generate_key(config.encrypted_cookie_salt, 32)
    sign_secret = key_generator.generate_key(config.encrypted_signed_cookie_salt)
    previous_format = ActiveSupport::MessageEncryptor.new(
      secret, sign_secret, :cipher => 'aes-256-cbc', :serializer => Marshal
    )

    session_data = previous_format.decrypt_and_verify(raw)
    assert_kind_of Hash, session_data
    assert_equal 2, session_data['user_id']
  end
end
EOF

steps.message: Rails 6.1 forwards all five settings into the request environment, so the pins take effect. Next I'll add them to `config/application.rb` as a single documented block, placed after the existing session store configuration.

arguments.command:
cd /app && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p = 'config/application.rb'
s = open(p).read()
anchor = "    config.session_store(\n"
block = """    # Rollback-safety pins (see docs/UPGRADE.md, "Framework-default pins").
    #
    # Redmine does not call config.load_defaults, so the values below are what
    # Rails uses today. Stating them explicitly keeps the format of session
    # cookies and of secret-derived values (such as the unwatch links in emails
    # already sent) the same as the previous release, which is the rollback
    # target. Rails 7.0's load_defaults would change these. Keep this block after
    # any load_defaults call so that the pins win.
    config.action_dispatch.cookies_serializer = :marshal
    config.action_dispatch.use_authenticated_cookie_encryption = false
    config.action_dispatch.use_cookies_with_metadata = false
    config.action_controller.per_form_csrf_tokens = false
    # Only Rails 7.0+ reads this setting. Rails 6.1 always derives keys with SHA1.
    config.active_support.key_generator_hash_digest_class = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1

"""
assert s.count(anchor) == 1
s = s.replace(anchor, block + anchor)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
EOF

steps.message: Rails 7.0 dropped the resolver-level `cached` method. Its `FileSystemResolver#_find_all` still caches unbound templates, so the lookup is still cached on 7.0. I'll make the patch version-aware: on 6.1 it keeps the existing `cached` path exactly, and on 7.0 it calls `_find_all` directly after the same `:api` format rewrite.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > /tmp/gen/resolver_old.txt <<'EOF'
  class Resolver
    def find_all(name, prefix=nil, partial=false, details={}, key=nil, locals=[])
      locals = locals.map(&:to_s).sort!.freeze

      cached(key, [name, prefix, partial], details, locals) do
        if (details[:formats] & [:xml, :json]).any?
          details = details.dup
          details[:formats] = details[:formats].dup + [:api]
        end
        _find_all(name, prefix, partial, details, key, locals)
      end
    end
  end
EOF
cat > /tmp/gen/resolver_new.txt <<'EOF'
  class Resolver
    def find_all(name, prefix=nil, partial=false, details={}, key=nil, locals=[])
      locals = locals.map(&:to_s).sort!.freeze

      # Rails 6.1 caches lookups in Resolver#cached. Rails 7.0 removed it and
      # caches unbound templates in FileSystemResolver instead.
      cacheable = private_method_defined?(:cached) || method_defined?(:cached)
      lookup = lambda do
        if (details[:formats] & [:xml, :json]).any?
          details = details.dup
          details[:formats] = details[:formats].dup + [:api]
        end
        _find_all(name, prefix, partial, details, key, locals)
      end

      if cacheable
        cached(key, [name, prefix, partial], details, locals, &lookup)
      else
        lookup.call
      end
    end
  end
EOF
ruby -e '
p = "config/initializers/10-patches.rb"
s = File.read(p)
old = File.read("/tmp/gen/resolver_old.txt")
new = File.read("/tmp/gen/resolver_new.txt")
raise "not found" unless s.scan(old).size == 1
File.write(p, s.sub(old) { new })
' && ruby -c config/initializers/10-patches.rb && git diff --stat

# Generates the artifacts a running release hands to users: a login session
# cookie, the anonymous CSRF token and form pair, and an unwatch mail link.
# Run it inside the release under test; ART_DIR chooses the output directory.
require File.join(ENV.fetch('APP_ROOT'), 'test/test_helper')

class ArtifactsGenTest < Redmine::IntegrationTest
  OUT = ENV.fetch('ART_DIR')

  def test_generate
    FileUtils.mkdir_p OUT
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = true
    travel_to Time.utc(2025, 1, 16, 12, 0, 0) do
      File.write("#{OUT}/mail_unwatch_token.txt", Mailer.mail_link_token(:unwatch, 'user_id' => 2, 'issue_id' => 1))

      get '/login'
      csrf = response.body[/name="authenticity_token" value="([^"]+)"/, 1]
      assert csrf.present?
      File.write("#{OUT}/csrf_token.txt", csrf)
      File.write("#{OUT}/csrf_cookie.txt", cookies['_redmine_session'])

      post '/login', :params => {:username => 'jsmith', :password => 'jsmith', :authenticity_token => csrf}
      assert_redirected_to '/my/page'
      get '/my/account'
      assert_response :success
      File.write("#{OUT}/session_cookie.txt", cookies['_redmine_session'])
      File.write("#{OUT}/session_tk.txt", Token.where(:user_id => 2, :action => 'session').order(:id).last.value)
    end
  ensure
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = false
  end
end
EOF
cat > /tmp/gen/sim/artifacts_read_test.rb <<'EOF'
# Reads artifacts written by another release and checks that this release
# still honours them: the session logs the user in, the unwatch link works,
# and the CSRF token from the other release is accepted on a form post.
require File.join(ENV.fetch('APP_ROOT'), 'test/test_helper')

class ArtifactsReadTest < Redmine::IntegrationTest
  fixtures :projects, :users, :email_addresses, :roles, :members, :member_roles,
           :trackers, :projects_trackers, :issue_statuses, :enumerations, :issues,
           :enabled_modules, :watchers, :tokens

  ART = ENV.fetch('ART_DIR')

  def art(name)
    File.read(File.join(ART, name)).strip
  end

  def test_session_cookie_still_logs_user_in
    travel_to Time.utc(2025, 1, 16, 12, 0, 0) do
      Token.insert_all!([{:user_id => 2, :action => 'session', :value => art('session_tk.txt'),
                          :created_on => Time.now, :updated_on => Time.now}])
      cookies['_redmine_session'] = art('session_cookie.txt')
      get '/my/account'
      assert_response :success
      assert_select '#loggedas', :text => /jsmith/
    end
  end

  def test_unwatch_link_still_works
    travel_to Time.utc(2025, 1, 16, 12, 0, 0) do
      Issue.find(1).set_watcher(User.find(2), true)
      get '/mail_links/unwatch', :params => {:token => art('mail_unwatch_token.txt')}
      assert_response :success
      assert_not Issue.find(1).watched_by?(User.find(2))
    end
  end

  def test_csrf_token_from_other_release_is_accepted
    return skip('no csrf artifacts') unless File.exist?(File.join(ART, 'csrf_token.txt'))
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = true
    cookies['_redmine_session'] = art('csrf_cookie.txt')
    post '/login', :params => {:username => 'jsmith', :password => 'wrong-password', :authenticity_token => art('csrf_token.txt')}
    assert_not_equal 422, response.status, 'CSRF token rejected (Redmine would sign the user out)'
  ensure
    ActionController::Base.allow_forgery_protection = false
  end
end
EOF

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /app/docs && cat > /app/docs/UPGRADE.md <<'EOF'
# Upgrade notes: Rails and Ruby

This file tracks the step-by-step move from Rails 6.1 to Rails 7.0 on
production. It records what each release has to stay compatible with, the
temporary framework-default overrides, and the work left for the next release.

Please keep it up to date with each release in this series.

## Release train

| Release | Ruby   | Rails      | Framework defaults                      | Role                                   |
|---------|--------|------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| R0      | 3.0.7  | 6.1.7.10   | none (`load_defaults` not called)       | Production before this series          |
| R1      | 3.2.9  | 6.1.7.10   | none (`load_defaults` not called)       | This release. Rollback target for R2   |
| R2      | 3.2.x  | 7.0.8.7    | `load_defaults "7.0"` plus overrides in section 4 | Next release                  |

Rollback means redeploying the previous release commit together with its own
`Gemfile.lock` (or `Gemfile.next.lock` for R2) and its Ruby version. No data
migration is involved.

## Rules

1. No release or rollback may sign anyone out. Session cookies, CSRF tokens
   that users already hold on open forms, and session tokens must keep working.
2. No release or rollback may break a link in a mail that was already sent.
   That covers the unwatch links, which are valid for 30 days.
3. A release must read everything the previous release wrote, and everything
   its rollback target would write, so that rolling back is safe at any time.
4. A release must write only formats that its rollback target can read.
   This is the reason for the pins in section 3.

## 1. What survives from one release to the next

| Data                                   | Where                              | Depends on the framework? | Checked by                                     |
|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Session cookie `_redmine_session`      | Browser. CookieStore, encrypted    | Yes (serializer, cipher, metadata, key derivation) | `test/integration/release_compatibility_test.rb` |
| Session token (`tokens`, `session`)    | Database                           | No                        | same                                           |
| Unwatch link in mail (`mail_links`)    | Sent mail. `message_verifier`      | Yes (key derivation, serializer, digest) | same                                           |
| CSRF tokens (forms, `_csrf_token`)     | Forms in browsers, session         | Yes (encoding, per-form tokens) | `artifacts_read_test` (sim, section 6)         |
| Autologin cookie `autologin`           | Browser. Plain, not signed         | No                        | Not affected                                   |
| `Rails.cache` (file store in `tmp/`)   | Disk, wiki/i18n/search caches      | Yes (cache format)        | Section 5 (cache format)                       |
| Encrypted DB columns (SCM, LDAP, TOTP) | Database. `Redmine::Ciphering`     | No. Uses OpenSSL with `database_cipher_key` | Not affected                |
| Hashed user passwords                  | Database. Redmine's own hash       | No                        | Not affected                                   |

### Where the secret comes from

Cookies and message verifiers are derived from `secret_key_base`. Rails reads it
from `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, from `config/credentials`, or from `config/secrets.yml`
(`rake generate_secret_token` writes `config/initializers/secret_token.rb` for
this). Never change that secret as part of an upgrade.

`secret_token` in `config/configuration.yml` is not read by Rails 6.1 or 7.0
(`config.secret_token` is set in `config/initializers/30-redmine.rb` but nothing
uses it). Changing it has no effect. It is left alone for now.

## 2. Compatibility decisions

- **D1. This release keeps writing the R0 formats.** R0 is the rollback target
  for R1, so R1 writes what R0 reads: the Marshal serializer, AES-256-CBC
  encrypted cookies, no cookie metadata, SHA1-derived keys, and global CSRF
  tokens. The pins in section 3 state this explicitly.
- **D2. This release reads the formats of R2's defaults.** Rails 6.1 already
  reads them: JSON-serialized cookies (`MarshalWithJsonFallback`), AES-256-GCM
  cookies (the `prepare_upgrade` path), cookies with purpose metadata, and urlsafe
  CSRF tokens. The round-trip tests in section 6 cover these.
- **D3. Ruby 3.2 is used for this release.** Ruby 3.0 and 3.2 produce the same
  Marshal, OpenSSL and PBKDF2 output, so the artifacts from R0 are read unchanged
  (see the golden tests). `Gemfile.lock` is resolved on Ruby 3.2, which selects
  nokogiri 1.18.9 as the Gemfile requires for Ruby 3.1 and later. The lock is
  per release, so rolling back to R0 uses R0's lock on Ruby 3.0.
- **D4. Redmine does not adopt `load_defaults` in this release.** Doing so would
  change several data formats at once. Adoption happens in R2 with overrides.
- **D5. Two Redmine patches needed changes for Rails 7.0 and are unchanged on
  Rails 6.1.** `config/initializers/10-patches.rb` overrides
  `ActionView::Resolver#find_all` to find the `*.api.*` templates. Rails 7.0 removed
  `cached` and matches templates against the requested details object. On 7.0
  only, `:api` is also a known template format, which the 7.0 resolver needs to
  parse `show.api.rsb`. It is not a MIME type, so request negotiation and `.api`
  URLs are unchanged.

## 3. Framework-default pins (this release)

`config/application.rb` pins the following values. Redmine never called
`load_defaults`, so these are the values Rails 6.1 already uses. The pins make
them explicit. A later `load_defaults "7.0"` placed above the pins cannot
override them.

| Setting                                                       | Value              | Rails 7.0 default under `load_defaults "7.0"` | Why it is pinned                                                       |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `action_dispatch.cookies_serializer`                          | `:marshal`         | `:json`                                       | R0 reads Marshal. JSON would turn the symbol-keyed session hashes (issue query filters, `auth_source_registration`) into string keys. |
| `action_dispatch.use_authenticated_cookie_encryption`         | `false`            | `true` (AES-256-GCM)                          | R0 reads only AES-256-CBC cookies.                                     |
| `action_dispatch.use_cookies_with_metadata`                   | `false`            | `true`                                        | R0 cannot read cookies that carry purpose metadata.                     |
| `action_controller.per_form_csrf_tokens`                      | `false`            | `true`                                        | R0 cannot validate per-form tokens. Redmine signs the user out on an invalid CSRF token. |
| `active_support.key_generator_hash_digest_class`              | `OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1` | `OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256`                | Changing the digest changes every derived key: sessions and unwatch links would stop working. Only Rails 7.0 reads this setting. |

When R2 switches to `load_defaults "7.0"`, the overrides it must keep are listed
in section 4.

## 4. Work left for the next release (R2)

Keep these overrides in R2 for as long as R1 is a rollback target. They sit
after `load_defaults "7.0"`:

- `cookies_serializer = :marshal`. Do not use `:json` or `:hybrid` yet. Rails
  7.0 rescues `JSON::ParserError` when it decrypts a cookie, so a Marshal cookie
  read by a JSON serializer is silently dropped and the user is signed out. JSON
  also loses the symbol keys of the session hashes (the issue query filters are
  read back with `[:id]` and `[:filters]`).
- `key_generator_hash_digest_class = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1`. Otherwise R1 cannot
  verify R2's session cookies or unwatch links, and R2 cannot verify those written
  by R1.
- `per_form_csrf_tokens = false`. R1 cannot validate per-form tokens.
- `active_support.cache_format_version = 6.1`. Rails 6.1 cannot read the 7.0
  cache entry format (`"\x00"` or `"\x01"` prefix). A rollback would fail on
  cache reads. The cache-format check in section 6 confirms this.

These are safe to keep on the 7.0 defaults, because R1 reads them:
`use_authenticated_cookie_encryption = true` and `use_cookies_with_metadata = true`.
`urlsafe_csrf_tokens` (7.0 default) is also read by R1.

Other changes that `load_defaults "7.0"` brings need checking and testing in R2
itself. They do not affect rollback data:

- `active_record.belongs_to_required_by_default` (5.0). Required associations
  could break saves.
- `action_controller.forgery_protection_origin_check` (5.0). A failed origin check
  counts as a CSRF failure, which signs the user out. Check behind reverse proxies
  before enabling it.
- `action_controller.raise_on_open_redirects` (7.0). External `redirect_to` raises.
- `action_controller.wrap_parameters_by_default` (7.0). JSON API bodies get
  wrapped. The REST API tests have to pass.
- `action_mailer.smtp_timeout = 5` (7.0). Slow SMTP servers could start failing.
- `active_record.partial_inserts = false`, `automatic_scope_inversing`,
  `has_many_inversing` (6.1 and 7.0).
- `active_support.hash_digest_class = SHA256` (7.0). Changes ETags and view and
  fragment cache keys only, so this causes cache misses, not data loss.
- `active_support.disable_to_s_conversion` (7.0).
- `action_dispatch.default_headers` (7.0). For example, `X-XSS-Protection: 0`.
- `ActiveRecord::Base.default_timezone` is deprecated in 7.0 and removed in 7.1.
  Redmine's `Query#date_clause` calls it. Use `ActiveRecord.default_timezone`
  behind a version check.
- Test fixtures use `to_s(:db)`, which 7.0 deprecates in favour of `to_fs(:db)`.
  `to_fs` does not exist on 6.1, so a version-neutral helper is needed.

Migration plan for later releases (outside R2, after R1 is retired):

1. Move `cookies_serializer` to `:json` only after session values are
   normalized to string keys and plain values. Convert the symbol-keyed hashes
   in `queries_helper.rb` and `account_controller.rb` first.
2. Move key derivation to SHA256 with a rotation that still reads the SHA1 keys,
   so sessions and mail links survive the change.
3. Remove `per_form_csrf_tokens = false` and the cache format pin once R1 is gone.

## 5. Rails 7.0 build (`Gemfile.next`)

- `Gemfile.next` is `Gemfile` with `rails 7.0.8.7`. Its lock, `Gemfile.next.lock`,
  was resolved from `Gemfile.lock` so that only the Rails 7.0 gems and what they
  require differ from production. Any other change to `Gemfile` must be made in
  `Gemfile.next` too.
- Use it with `BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bundle install`. `config/boot.rb`
  respects `BUNDLE_GEMFILE`.
- The Rails 7.0 build runs with the same configuration as R1, meaning without
  `load_defaults`. Its formats are then identical to R1's.
- Rails 7.0 changes found while getting the suite to run and then fixed:
  - `ActionView::Resolver#find_all` (`10-patches.rb`), described in D5.
  - `:api` as a template format on 7.0 only.

## 6. Verification

Compatibility tests:

- `test/integration/release_compatibility_test.rb` uses golden artifacts written by
  R0 (Rails 6.1, Ruby 3.0.7, commit `ba6dc56`) in `test/fixtures/files/upgrade/`.
  They are a session cookie with its session token, and an unwatch link. The tests
  check that the user stays logged in, that the link still unsubscribes, and that
  R1 still writes the R0 cookie format.
- Mutation check: changing `cookies_serializer` to `:json`,
  `use_authenticated_cookie_encryption` to `true`, or `use_cookies_with_metadata`
  to `true` makes the tests fail.
- The golden artifacts must not be regenerated for an existing release. They
  stay as they are. A new release adds its own files.

Results on the current code:

- Ruby 3.2.9, Rails 6.1.7.10 (`bin/rails test`): RESULT_62
- Ruby 3.2.9, Rails 7.0.8.7 with `Gemfile.next` (`BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bin/rails test`): RESULT_70

SIM_PLACEHOLDER

## 7. Notes for the next release

- R2 must not drop the tests in section 6. Add golden artifacts that R1 writes,
  and check that R2 can read them and that R1 can read R2's output.
- `config/initializers/10-patches.rb` gets a branch for Rails 7.0 only. Once R1 is
  retired, keep only the 7.0 code path.
- The fixtures' `to_s(:db)` must become a version-neutral helper before 6.1 is
  dropped.
EOF

On 6.1 the template format stays unset, so the request's format is used. The cleaner fix is to make 7.0's parser read `show.api.rsb` as `show` with no format, which is what 6.1 effectively does, and to restore the 6.1 patch to its original R0 form. steps.message: The nil format is included in each index hash as the lowest-priority match, so a template parsed with no format matches any requested format, as it does on 6.1. I'll restore `10-patches.rb` to its original R0 text and make the change version-specific. On 6.1 the `find_all` patch is the R0 code unchanged. On 7.0 a small prepended parser patch replaces the resolver patch and the `:api` type registration.

arguments.command:
cd /app && git show HEAD:config/initializers/10-patches.rb > /tmp/gen/10-patches.R0.rb && cat > /tmp/gen/resolver_v2.txt <<'EOF'
  if Rails.gem_version < Gem::Version.new('7.0')
    class Resolver
      def find_all(name, prefix=nil, partial=false, details={}, key=nil, locals=[])
        locals = locals.map(&:to_s).sort!.freeze

        cached(key, [name, prefix, partial], details, locals) do
          if (details[:formats] & [:xml, :json]).any?
            details = details.dup
            details[:formats] = details[:formats].dup + [:api]
          end
          _find_all(name, prefix, partial, details, key, locals)
        end
      end
    end
  else
    class Resolver
      # Rails 7.0 only recognizes registered formats in template file names, so
      # the API views (show.api.rsb) would be parsed as "show.api" and not found.
      # Drop the .api part before parsing. The template then matches any format,
      # as it does on Rails 6.1.
      module ApiTemplateNames
        def parse(path)
          super(path.sub(/\.api(?=\.[^.\/]+\z)/, ''))
        end
      end
      PathParser.prepend(ApiTemplateNames)
    end
  end
EOF

    travel_to GOLDEN_TIME do

  end

steps.message: The R1 artifacts are recorded, and its CSRF token is standard base64, as expected for 6.1. Next I'll create the two simulated next-release copies. `r2min` uses `load_defaults "7.0"` with only the overrides I've identified as necessary (Marshal serializer, SHA1 key digest, per-form CSRF off, cache format 6.1). `r2none` uses `load_defaults "7.0"` with no overrides at all.

arguments.command:
for v in r2min r2none; do rm -rf /tmp/$v; cp -a /tmp/r2sim /tmp/$v; done && cat > /tmp/gen/make_variant.rb <<'EOF'
# usage: ruby make_variant.rb <dir> <min|none>
dir, variant = ARGV
p = File.join(dir, 'config/application.rb')
s = File.read(p)
pins_start = s.index("    # Rollback-safety pins")
pins_end = s.index("    config.session_store(")
raise 'pins block not found' unless pins_start && pins_end
pins = s[pins_start...pins_end]
case variant
when 'min'
  pins = pins.lines.reject { |l| l =~ /use_authenticated_cookie_encryption|use_cookies_with_metadata/ }.join
  pins += "    config.active_support.cache_format_version = 6.1\n\n"
  s = s[0...pins_start] + "    config.load_defaults '7.0'\n\n" + pins + s[pins_end..]
when 'none'
  s = s[0...pins_start] + "    config.load_defaults '7.0'\n\n" + s[pins_end..]
else
  raise 'variant'
end
File.write(p, s)
EOF
